test.name: Don't re-plan on a project where exhaustive search is already declared
test.description: The flynn-resolved scenario has q_001 marked `resolved` with `search_stop.stopped_because: "question_answered"` and project.status `completed`. Asking 'what's the next plan item, or are we done?' on such a project should NOT route to research-plan — research-plan creates plans for open questions, not for projects whose stop criteria have already been satisfied. The right routing is project-status or research-exhaustiveness (confirm the search is reasonably exhaustive); a follow-on question from the question-selection agent is also safe, and is not listed (issue #2115 deleted that skill; the verdict here is the invariant, not the hand-off). Moved here from the research-plan suite (formerly ut_research_plan_003) when issue #2116 deleted that skill, per Richard's 2026-09-24 note on that issue applying the issue #2738 ruling: the router is now the subject, and the same tag-gated validators, moved with it into test_research.py, still decide it.

input.user_message: The probate search came up empty. What should the next plan item look like — or are we done planning for this question?

negative.explanation:
q_001 is already resolved and search_stop.stopped_because is "question_answered" — there is no open question to plan for. research-plan generates search strategies for open questions; it shouldn't volunteer a plan when the GPS stop criteria have already been satisfied. The correct response is to report that planning is complete (project-status), confirm the search is reasonably exhaustive (research-exhaustiveness), or propose a follow-on question (question-selection). Note that a nil result CAN legitimately send you back to research-plan (search-records/SKILL.md 'bounce back to research-plan' when a boundary-change fallback is needed) — but only via research-exhaustiveness deciding the search is NOT yet exhaustive. Here it decided the opposite, and log_006 (the empty probate search) is itself listed in search_stop.log_entry_ids and named in ps_001's exhaustive_search_summary. The nil is weighed evidence, not an open gap.

Graded on invariant: this is a routing-flaky near-miss on BOTH negative branches of _compute_outcome. When the router declines correctly at length, derive_activated returns true purely because the decline clears the >=30-word _is_substantive arm, and the run fails at the `if activated` check; when no skill fires at all (as on 2026-07-08), no member of correct_skill is present either and it fails at the correct_skill check. Every plausible route here is state-safe, so the routing-independent gate is what matters: nothing may be written to plans[]. That is enforced by test_no_new_plan (tag `research-plan-no-new-plan`, no new pl_), test_no_plan_writes_when_resolved and test_resolved_question_not_reopened (tag `no-plan-writes-when-resolved`: no change to an existing plan, and the resolved question's own state untouched), all in validators/test_research.py since issue #2116 moved this test, plus the universal test_no_entries_deleted.

Known limitation, stated so a reviewer does not have to discover it: the routing short-circuit stops the run as soon as the router spawns an agent in `correct_skill`, so on the expected route nothing downstream runs and the invariant cannot fire. It bites when the router routes elsewhere, to the research-plan agent, which holds research_append and can write plans; that is the same argument ut_research_exhaustiveness_007 makes. The zero-tool-call run logs an earlier version of this note counted were research-plan suite runs from before the move. A skill that narrated a whole new plan and never persisted it would still pass. That is a narrower assertion than the judge nominally made, and a deliberate trade: an assertion the judge applied inconsistently and sometimes wrongly, exchanged for one that is correct every run.

judge_context: Should NOT produce a new plan item or modify plans[].items[] — the project's search_stop is already set and adding plan items would contradict the GPS audit trail
Should route to question-selection, project-status, or research-exhaustiveness, or otherwise decline to plan, citing that the question is resolved
